findings.title: Flexbox on .small-action unpins the action button and shrink-wraps the description
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex container (display:flex via the new flexbox mixin, align-items:center), and .small-action-desc is no longer a full-width block. Its padding changed from 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em to 0 1.5%, and it has no flex-grow, so it shrink-wraps to its text. The staff delete/recover control is positioned only by .small-action button { float: right }, which used to pin it to the right edge of that full-width row. Float does not apply to flex items, so a button that is a direct child stays in source order beside the label; a button nested in .small-action-desc only floats to the right of the shrink-wrapped description, not the post row. On short actions the control sits against or over the label instead of at the far right. Set flex: 1 and min-width: 0 on .small-action-desc so an inner float can still reach the row edge, or drop the float and push the button with margin-left: auto.

findings.title: order() mixin is off by one for 2009 box-ordinal-group
findings.body: order() writes $val straight through to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1, legal values are integers >= 1); standard order is 0-based (initial value 0). The matching prefix is $val + 1. As written, order(0) emits box-ordinal-group: 0, which is invalid and dropped so the item stays in the default group; order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of following them; a negative order, the usual way to pull an item to the front, is invalid and ignored. -ms-flex-order and -webkit-order correctly share order's numbering, so IE10 and 2012-spec WebKit are fine. Header callers pass 2 and 3, which still sort after default items in both systems, but the mixin does not implement order for any other value. Add 1 on the two box-ordinal-group declarations.

findings.title: align-items() mixin emits an invalid property and skips old Firefox
findings.body: align-items() copies one keyword into every prefix and emits -ms-align-items, which is not a CSS property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, already set above). Old Firefox, which flexbox() and inline-flex() target with display: -moz-box and display: -moz-inline-box, needs -moz-box-align, and that declaration is missing. Header .contents, .small-action, and .badge-wrapper.bullet therefore become 2009 boxes with no cross-axis alignment in that engine, so the vertical centering and bullet baseline alignment this PR adds do not apply. The 2009 and IE10 properties also do not accept modern keywords: flex-start and flex-end must be mapped to start and end for -webkit-box-align, -moz-box-align, and -ms-flex-align, while -webkit-align-items and align-items keep the modern names. center and baseline happen to be valid in all three syntaxes, so IE10 and old WebKit align for the current call sites, but the mixin is wrong for the other standard values.

findings.title: Header panel is not pinned right in the 2009 flexbox the new mixin enables
findings.body: .d-header .panel no longer has float: right, and .d-header .title no longer has float: left. The replacement is margin-left: auto on .panel inside a .contents flex container, plus order. Auto margins absorb free space in modern flexbox and in IE10 (-ms-flexbox), so current Chrome, Firefox, Safari 7+, and IE10 still pin the icons to the right. They do not in the 2009 model: display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box, which the new flexbox() mixin emits, treat auto margins as 0 and only distribute space with box-flex / -webkit-box-flex, which is never set. Browsers that only understand those prefixes (Safari 6, iOS 6, Android 4.3 stock browser, Firefox 21 and older) pack the logo, topic info, and controls on the left instead of keeping the menu at the right edge. Browsers with no flexbox at all lose the float fallback and stack the logo and panel as normal blocks. Keep float: left / float: right as the non-flex fallback (a flex formatting context ignores float on the items) and drop the 2009 display values, or add a 2009 pack so those prefixes actually reproduce the header.
